newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips dip on sale, index ends higher.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips dip on sale, index ends higher.

text.p: Prices of some blue chips fell on Wednesday on selling but the all-share index rose to 7139.89 from 7122.11 on Tuesday.
On offer were stocks of top conglomerates, brewers, cement and textile manufacturing companies.
Lever Brothers closed at 18.25 naira and Nigerian Breweries at 16.50 naira, each dropping 50 kobo.
Ashaka Cement recorded its heaviest one-day fall, finishing 78 kobo down at 14.82 naira. Dealers said the stock would hover around 10.00 naira before experiencing any turnaround.
But West African Portland Cement Company was different, closing 50 kobo higher at 50.00 naira on rising buy order.
Growing interest took Cadbury to 22.60 naira, up 50 kobo and UAC to 8.35 naira, up 15 kobo while Dunlop gained a modest two kobo to 7.55 naira.
Oil and foods shares advanced strongly as demand for them far outweighed supply.
Unipetrol remained the dearest stock on the exchange closing at 64.34 naira, up 71 kobo.
